capabilities.target: Private repositories owned by the user (reachable via the broadly scoped PAT)

inputs.source: User's direct chat prompt in the desktop client
Issue content and comments in the public GitHub repository, authorable by any GitHub user

instructions.evidence_locator: runtime notes: user prompt 'Have a look at the open issues in my public repo.'
instructions.note: The instruction does not constrain the agent to read-only actions or to the public repository alone. Combined with a credential that reaches every repository the user owns and a create_pull_request capability, the agent is architecturally able to go far beyond 'have a look'.

controls.name: Per tool call approval prompt (collapsed arguments)
controls.decay_rationale: The approver reviews a collapsed, model-summarized view of each tool call rather than the raw destination and payload. A more persuasive model, and the noted pattern of approving many calls per session, both reduce effective scrutiny (ASI09 / approval fatigue).

controls.name: Per-repository scoped credential (no cross-repo broad PAT)
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to only the public repository, with no private-repo read access, would make it impossible for the agent to retrieve confidential content regardless of model behavior or approval outcomes, severing the lethal-trifecta path.

controls.name: Pinned/hashed MCP server image
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the server image to a specific digest and verifying publisher signatures prevents silent supply-chain tampering (rug pulls) independent of model capability.

controls.name: Pre-publish secret/content scanning before cross-repo write
controls.decay_rationale: A content scanner catches obvious secrets but can be evaded through encoding, paraphrase, or partial-content leakage, so it narrows rather than severs the path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): malicious public issue drives confidential private-repo read and public PR egress via over-broad PAT

attack_path.note: An attacker-authored issue in the public repository contains hidden instructions (indirect prompt injection) that the agent reads while looking at open issues.
Directed by the injected instructions, the agent uses the single broad GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN to call get_file_contents on the user's private repositories.
The agent creates a pull request on the public repository that embeds the private repository's confidential content, publishing it outside the trust boundary.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Approval setting changed to auto-approve / 'always allow' for this tool; client upgraded to show only a one-line summary instead of full arguments; or a rising approval click-through rate as session call volume grows (approval fatigue).

evidence.observation: A single GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN env var is passed to the server with repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private — not scoped per repository.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository.'
evidence.observation: Confirms the issue content is attacker-reachable (untrusted) input the agent will read while completing the stated task.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: 'The client asks for approval per tool call. Arguments are collapsed by default. Users approve many calls per session.'
evidence.observation: The only preventive control is a per-call approval gate in model_summary mode subject to approval fatigue, which the rubric floors at moderate residual rather than crediting as a severing control.

recommendations.action: Scope credentials per repository or use fine-grained GitHub App installation tokens limited to the specific repository in scope for a given task; remove private-repo read access from any credential an agent uses while working on public-repo issues.
Set the approval UI to raw_action review for any capability reachable from untrusted content: show the full destination repository, visibility, and diff before create_pull_request executes.
Scan PR content for secrets or private-repo markers before publishing, and alert on any cross-repository data movement from a private to a public target.

findings.title: Unpinned MCP server image (ASI04): github-mcp-server pulled without a digest or signature pin

attack_path.note: The docker run command pulls ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest pin, so the exact image served can change silently between runs.
A compromised or rug-pulled server build runs with the full broad PAT already mounted, so it can read or exfiltrate the token independent of the agent's own behavior.
A compromised build could also push data out through any write capability it is handed, bypassing the per-call approval gate entirely.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

evidence.observation: No tag or digest is specified, so the image resolves to whatever 'latest' points to at pull time; nothing in the artifacts pins or verifies the image.

evidence.locator: runtime notes: broad PAT passed via -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
evidence.observation: The container that would run a tampered build already holds the full-scope token, with no separate confirmation step covering actions the server code itself might take outside the agent's visible tool calls.

This path's 'source' is the MCP server supply chain rather than a declared input. Inherent risk is set to high rather than critical because a supply-chain compromise is a precondition rather than simply attacker-authored content, and likelihood is correspondingly lower (unlikely).

recommendations.action: Pin the server image to a specific content digest, verify publisher signatures before pulling, and gate updates through a review step.
Run the container with an explicit network egress allowlist so a tampered server build cannot reach destinations beyond the GitHub API.

rating.rationale: The dominant path is the lethal trifecta: an attacker-authored public GitHub issue (untrusted) is read by the agent, which then uses a single over-broad personal access token to read confidential private-repo content and publish it via a public pull request (irreversible egress). Inherent risk is critical (untrusted source, severe/irreversible sink). The only present control is a per-tool-call approval prompt that shows a collapsed, model-summarized view rather than the raw destination and payload, which the rubric floors at moderate residual rather than crediting as path-severing, especially given the noted pattern of high per-session approval volume (approval fatigue, ASI09). Because that gate is partially_dependent on model behavior, it is expected to fail first under a model upgrade, an autonomy increase, or simple removal/loosening of the prompt, restoring the critical inherent exposure — this is the forecast. A secondary, lower-confidence finding flags the unpinned MCP server container image as an ASI04 supply-chain exposure that the approval gate does not cover at all, since a tampered server binary could act on the same broad credential independently of the agent's visible tool calls. The single highest-leverage fix is scoping the GitHub credential per repository so the private-repo read is structurally unreachable from a public-repo task, which would sever the primary path outright.

output_consumers: public GitHub repository (pull requests, visible to anyone)

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration (the MCP server config and runtime notes provided), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest or MCP tools/list response was provided; tool descriptions were not reviewed for embedded instructions (SAFE-T1001 Tool Poisoning), so that check could not be completed and confidence on tool-level findings is reduced.
No system prompt was provided beyond the single user request shown; any additional guardrail instructions the deployment may add are unknown and are not credited as controls here.

Whether the private repositories actually contain restricted-sensitivity data (e.g., credentials) was not confirmed; consequence for finding f1 is rated at the confidential/major level rather than restricted/severe pending that confirmation.
